summary: A 1977 unsanitized IG report, released under the JFK Assassination Records Act, on plots to assassinate Fidel Castro. Prepared at the DCI's request by Inspector General J.S. Earman, delivered to DCI Richard Helms in 1967 installments. Helms returned the copy May 22, 1967 with instructions: keep the one copy in personal safekeeping, destroy the other copy and all notes and source materials; the text was destroyed May 23, 1967 and only this text remains. Signed by Helms, Earman, Greer and Breckinridge. Source materials included Office of Security files, memoranda on William Harvey and certain Mafia figures, and Drew Pearson columns. Handling records show it was reviewed by House Select Committee staff.

summary: The page states that the aggressive scheme to be launched in August 1962 was first conceived in early 1960 and revived in 1963, but nothing came of it. Officers felt intense pressure from the Agency's responsible leadership to act against the Cuban regime, and the plotting is judged unrealistic in retrospect. Interviewees stressed two points: eliminating a dominant figure does not necessarily topple a government, and an October 1961 draft paper held that Castro's demise would offer little opportunity to liberate Cuba from Communist and Soviet control. Removing a government's leaders is also necessary to bring about its downfall.

nodes.title: Ski:. Siving Suit
nodes.summary: The text describes a CIA-era plot, around the Donovan-Castro negotiations over the Bay of Pigs prisoners, to present Fidel Castro, a skin-diving enthusiast, with a contaminated diving suit as a gift. The suit was to be dusted with a fungus causing disabling chronic skin disease (Madura foot) and its breathing apparatus contaminated with tubercle bacilli. Accounts differ on its origin (under William Harvey or after Desmond FitzGerald took over the Cuba task force in January 1963), and Sidney Gottlieb said a suit was bought and readied. Samuel Halpern said it was dropped as impracticable, later that Donovan had independently given Castro a diving suit. Halpern also said he mentioned the plan to George McManus, who told Helms. Named participants include Richard Helms, William Harvey, Desmond FitzGerald, Samuel Halpern, George McManus, Sidney Gottlieb, and Ray Treichler.

summary: The text is an OCR-degraded excerpt from an inquiry into who leaked a story about a gambling syndicate operation (Pearson column). It concludes Bill Harvey is unlikely the source: he knew all four key facts, had no clear motive, and would not be so indiscreet, and a Harvey leak would make the story accurate. The State Department meeting was known to no other participants, suggesting at least two leak sources. John Roselli, the only continuous participant across both phases, is the next likely source; he knew Edwards' identity and Edwards' claim of briefing Attorney General Kennedy, possibly leading Roselli to infer Kennedy's role. Robert Maheu's knowledge is uncertain, with firsthand knowledge of phase one but probably little of phase two, which may have come from Roselli. Maceo, Roselli's associate in phase two, and Varona's knowledge are also considered.

summary: OCR-garbled excerpt from a declassified intelligence document (SS14-0000) discussing the sourcing of a Drew Pearson story. It covers who had direct knowledge of the operation, including Giancana and Trafficante presumably being excluded from Phase Two, with Roselli as the likely ultimate source. It suggests the immediate sources were differing people leaking or peddling the story with ulterior motives, which were hard to determine, and notes a State Department meeting and a gambling syndicate as possible informants.

summary: OCR-garbled excerpt from a 1967-era intelligence memo (document 14-0000) on the Pearson/Roselli-Morgan story about a CIA-linked plot against Castro. It discusses who knew what: Giancana and Trafficante likely excluded from the operation, Roselli as the probable ultimate source, and Morgan and Maheu as channels. It covers the leak's likely motives (drinking and loose talk), the Roselli-Garrison meeting in Las Vegas in March, and Garrison's suspected Castro-retaliation theory. It also notes Pearson's unused material, Garrison's undisclosed case, and Philippine and Puerto Rican claims about a Castro speech threatening Kennedy.

summary: OCR-garbled 1960s-era memo (file 14-0000) on Las Vegas and Garrison investigation matters. Covers: Garrison's Las Vegas conference and alleged Castro-Kennedy assassination retaliation plots (unconfirmed); Drew Pearson's unused material (pills, State Department meeting); Garrison's unrevealed case and expected CIA involvement; Philippine and Puerto Rican claims about a Castro speech, with no record found; handling of Roselli, Varona, and the Bay of Pigs; Giancana, Trafficante, and Fosellia's fallen status; cover story of U.S. business sponsors; and Morgan's attorney-client role.

title: 4. Pearson,
summary: The text is an OCR-garbled excerpt from a 1975 CIA document about the Agency's plot to assassinate Fidel Castro (Phase One and Phase Two, 1960-1962) using mafia intermediaries such as Johnny Roselli and Sam Giancana. It covers the Pearson newspaper story and its threat to Howard Hughes's interests, what Attorney General Robert Kennedy was briefed on, and whether other components of government know of the operation. It also weighs whether the story can be suppressed, the risks of approaching participants, and the need for an independent investigation. The memo concludes that the story cannot be suppressed and that personal approaches would only add credence to it.
